title: Complexity of Hard-Intervention Compatibility for Partial Ancestral Graphs
banked_reason: The cap is not clearable: source-faithful XREG semantics require re-proving both headline claims, and theorem-level overlap with the closest 2026 controlled-soft result remains unresolved.
gap_reasons: XREG(I,J;Y,X,W) never specifies its conditional-law equality or graphical separation, so HARD-EXTEND is not defined for general legal XREG records beyond the special X=W=empty reduction use.
The cited h-faithfulness definition takes converses of the source’s specific I-Markov constraints; it does not support the proposal’s unrestricted signed XREG grammar with an additional X argument.

The closest controlled-soft completion paper is publicly identified as ICML 2026, but inspectable theorem text was unavailable, so its realizability/completion result cannot yet be rigorously separated from the proposed hard-language frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: The run developed five versions of a hard-intervention common-realizer/completion proposal, then pivoted to a HARD-EXTEND hardness-versus-tractability frontier and granted one non-identical retry. The final proposal still used an unsupported XREG language and lacked proofs that its clause gadget and FPT boundary summaries survive source-faithful semantics; field novelty also remained unresolved against the closest 2026 controlled-soft completion theorem. A future retry must first prove the hard-surgery gadget and tractable boundary in an exact source-supported language, then complete a theorem-level overlap or non-transfer audit.
tldr: The revised project asks for a sharp complexity phase transition for literal partial hard-intervention compatibility. Its precise candidate is that HARD-EXTEND is NP-complete already for an explicit multi-regime clause-channel fragment in which perfect surgery decides whether a targeted selector edge survives and a negative XREG atom demands a surviving clause path, while the same problem is fixed-parameter tractable for laminar target menus whose signed-record factor graph has bounded treewidth and whose latent-confounding envelope has bounded districts. This would separate genuinely global hard-surgery coupling from CI-only compatibility and provide a constructive witness algorithm on a nontrivial class with arbitrarily many variables and regimes.
gap: The hard-intervention literature defines the forward augmented signature and a sound incomplete orientation procedure, but it does not classify the encoded partial-extension language. COmbINE supplies exact SAT-based compatibility for within-regime CI information, not a lower bound driven by target-dependent hard deletion and signed cross-regime inequalities. No inspected work gives a parameterized common-realizer algorithm that simultaneously retains latent districts, multiple hard regimes, and signed XREG factors.
fill: Prove polynomial witness verification, the explicit selector/channel truth table, and the resulting NP-completeness theorem; then prove a finite separator congruence and a witness-producing FPT dynamic program for laminar targets, bounded factor-incidence treewidth, and bounded bidirected-capable districts. Both halves are required for success.
